question_record.context: A recent command and control behavior was blocked on the host `vnevado-win10s`. The host made a suspicious request using `curl http://vectorsandarrows.com`, and this suspicious activity could be associated with malware capable of receiving commands from remote attackers. Additionally, because the malware was active, higher severity ratings were assigned, and precautionary measures were recommended to prevent further infection.
question_record.question: Following up on this incident, ransomware-like behavior was observed. Could you identify the file name that was associated with this ransomware attempt?
solution: Malware with command and control behavior was detected and blocked on the account `dp5hn`.
A potentially compromised asset exhibited ransomware-like behavior with the file `syncretic.7z.lockbit`.

106.name: Command and Control behavior was blocked
106.description:
Malware and unwanted software are undesirable applications that perform annoying, disruptive, or harmful actions on affected machines. Some of these undesirable applications can replicate and spread from one machine to another. Others are able to receive commands from remote attackers and perform activities associated with cyber attacks.

A malware is considered active if it is found running on the machine or it already has persistence mechanisms in place. Active malware detections are assigned higher severity ratings.

Because this malware was active, take precautionary measures and check for residual signs of infection.

147.name: Potentially compromised assets exhibiting ransomware-like behavior
147.description: Potentially compromised assets are exhibiting ransomware-like behavior, impacting several devices. An attacker may be operating using the specified user account, IP, or device to move laterally across the network and infect as many devices as possible with ransomware. Automated remediation action might be taken to disable the account or device the attacker used.

interpretation.scope: official graph witness, not a proof of causality, actor identity or autonomous planning

steps.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT o.AlertId, o.AlertTitle, o.ObservedAt, o.EntityIndex,
       o.GraphValue AS value, o.RawComponents, o.Roles, o.SourceRowHash,
       i.GraphValue AS matched_input
FROM LTMInputEvidence i
JOIN LTMEntityEvidence o ON o.SourceRowHash = i.SourceRowHash
WHERE i.AlertTitle = %s
  AND i.Concept = 'Device_AAD_ID' AND o.Concept = 'Account_Name'
  AND i.GraphValue IN (%s)
ORDER BY o.AlertId, o.SourceRowHash, o.EntityIndex, o.GraphValue, i.GraphValue
LIMIT 501
